This is the first bail application filed by the applicant under Section 439 of the Code of Criminal Procedure for grant of regular bail relating to Crime No.161/2024 registered at Police Station - Raisen, District Raisen (M.P.) for the offences punishable under Sections 363, 366, 376(2)(N) of IPC and Section 5(L)/6 of POCSO Act.

Applicant is in detention since 14.04.2024.
2.
As per the prosecution story, in short, the victim left her home without informing her parents.
A missing report was lodged by the parents stating that present applicant had taken their daughter away and committed rape with her daughter on the false pretext of marriage.
On the basis of aforesaid, Police registered the case against the present applicant and other persons under the aforesaid Sections.

sentences.text: Learned counsel for the applicant submitted that applicant is in jail since 14.04.2024.
Applicant is lady aged about 50 years.
She has no role in the present alleged offence.
Applicant was residing at Indore.
Prosecutrix herself came from Raisen to Indore.
She has been falsely implicated in the case.
Charge sheet has been filed.
There is no criminal record of the applicant.
Therefore, it has been prayed that the applicant may be released on bail.
4. On the other hand, learned Panel Lawyer and Objector has opposed the prayer for grant of bail to the applicant.
5. Having taken into consideration all the facts and circumstances of the case, but without commenting on merit of the case, I am inclined to release the applicant on bail.
Consequently, bail application under Section 439 of the Code o f Criminal Procedure for grant of bail filed on behalf of applicant, stands allowed.

6. It is directed that applicant be released on bail on her furnishing a personal bond in the sum of Rs.50,000/- (Rupees Fifty Thousand only) with one solvent surety in the like amount to the satisfaction of the trial Court, for her regular appearance before the trial Court during trial with a condition that she shall remain present before the concerned Court on all the dates fixed by it during trial.

She shall abide by all the conditions enumerated under Section 437(3) of Cr.P.C.
7.
This order shall be effective till the end of the trial.
However, in case of bail jump and breach of any of the conditions of bail, it shall become ineffective.
Certified copy as per rules.

(PRAMOD KUMAR AGRAWAL) JUDGE Shub Smt. Savitri Bai vs The State Of Madhya Pradesh on 15 May, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/179633388/
